correctness.rationale: With sensitivity \(s\) and specificity \(c\), balanced accuracy is \(B=(s+c)/2\), squared G-mean is \(G^2=sc\), and \(G^2=B^2-(s-c)^2/4\). Exact exhaustive enumeration of every positive-cell, above-chance, fixed-prevalence table through \(N=11\) verifies no strict reversal for \(N\le10\) and exactly six at \(N=11\), including the stated rational witness values.

value.rationale: Balanced accuracy and sensitivity-specificity G-mean are standard summaries for imbalanced binary classification. Fixing both prevalence and test-set size and excluding chance-or-worse and zero-cell cases makes the disagreement scientifically interpretable rather than a trivial degeneracy. The exact minimum and the identity \(G^2=B^2-\delta^2\) quantify when unequal class performance is strong enough to overturn arithmetic-mean ranking.
